newsitem.title: BELGIUM: DESIGNER VERSACE LOSES TRADEMARK CASE IN BELGIUM.
newsitem.headline: DESIGNER VERSACE LOSES TRADEMARK CASE IN BELGIUM.

text.p: Leading Italian fashion house Gianni Versace on Thursday lost a Belgian court case against a woman who had been selling fashion accessories with its world registered trademark, the head of snake-haired gorgon Medusa.
It was unclear immediately if the decision by the court in the port city of Antwerp would have implications outside Belgium and, if so, how much it could eventually cost Versace.
Companies spend heavily on creating trademarks and fight strenuously to protect them. A conspicuous trademark is a strong selling point.

Milan-based Versace launched the court case through the Belgian copyright protection association, accusing the woman of selling scarves, bags and belts with a Medusa logo that were not made by or licensed to Versace.
The Antwerp court threw out the company's case. It gave no reasons for its decision.
The woman had argued that mythological characters were part of world culture and therefore could not be appropriated for the exclusive use of private businesses.
